decisions.reason: As a training offer that builds on the firm's existing service capabilities and customer-support strategy, it is relatively visible and strategically coherent, so management is inclined to retain it and view any weakness as temporary.

This accessory fits the installed machine base and supports the core offering, but because it required less public commitment and likely lower sunk investment than a full machine line, it is somewhat easier to discontinue if demand stays soft.

Although management may want to justify the R&D behind this future-oriented concept, its greater distance from the established offer and weaker public commitment make it the most likely candidate to be taken off the market.

A multi-model high-speed CNC milling line is highly invested, highly visible, and central to the firm's declared direction in advanced production solutions, so escalation of commitment strongly favors continuing it.

Because this automatic tool change system builds directly on the firm's established machinery business and was presented prominently, management is likely to keep backing it as a complementary productivity upgrade.
